name: floating-navbar

frames.best_why: Navbar is fully visible and centred over dark content without covering the heading.

tagline: Menu bar that slides away as you read and floats back when you scroll up.
summary: A fixed pill of four text links with a Login button. It sits at the top of the viewport and hides while the page scrolls down, sliding back into view the moment you scroll up.
appearance: One slim, fully rounded pill floating at the top centre of the page, holding four small text links separated by a thin divider from a filled Login button. It has a soft shadow and a translucent backdrop.
behaviour: It is absent at the top and whenever the page scrolls down. Scrolling up brings it back with a quick slide and fade from above, and the links lighten under the pointer.
demo_content: Hero headline The navbar hides while you read, then four numbered sections on design systems.
search_phrases: menu that hides when scrolling down
header that appears on scroll up
sticky menu bar with login button
use_when: Long marketing pages where readers want the navigation out of the way until they need it.
avoid_when: Hidden at the very top, so first-time visitors see no navigation until they scroll.
customise: navItems supplies a name, link and optional icon per entry; the Login label, colours and scroll thresholds are written in the source.
weight_why: One animated pill driven by scroll progress; nothing runs when idle.

a11y.note: On small screens links collapse to icons with no text label, and no focus-visible styling is added.

issues: When it reappears it overlaps the section heading in frames 3 and 6.
No focus-visible styling beyond the browser default.
At the top of the page no navigation is visible at all.
polish_why: Tidy pill with a clear slide-in; it reappears over body text and relies on default focus rings.
title: Floating Navbar
